title: fix(plugin-list): refuse a non-positive `pageSize` before it reaches the wire (objectui#9897)
body:
Part of #9897

⚠️ **`Part of`, not a closing keyword.** The read point named on the card is
repaired and the whole fence is green, but two things survive this merge and are
named at the foot of this body: the card's own **FIFTH default** is declared
rather than settled, and a **SIXTH site** of this same defect class was measured
outside this fence and is reported rather than touched. The seat closes the card
when it has an answer for those.

## What this changes

`ListView` resolved one authored `pagination.pageSize` with a bare `??` chain.
`??` rejects only `null` and `undefined`, so an authored `pageSize: 0` was not
nullish and survived as a real page size. All of it now goes through one
resolver, mirroring what objectui#9853 landed on `ObjectGrid` — *one resolver at
every entry is what keeps the answer single*.

### ⭐ The card said "three consumers". Re-derived on the tip this branch was cut
from (`fc12bc8c6`), the value is read at **one** point and feeds **six**

| consumer | what it does with the resolved value |
|:--|:--|
| the fetch window | `$top` on the wire |
| the window step | the `$skip` multiplier that turns the page |
| the has-more gate | `items.length` compared against it, behind the "showing first N" cap |
| the child grid | handed down as its `pageSize` under `manualPagination` |
| the record cap | the number printed in the data-limit banner |
| the rows-per-page control | its own displayed value |

⭐ **The card's structural framing does not survive, and the reading wins.** The
sibling had the value spelled out separately at three read points with three
different operators; here there is exactly **ONE** read point. The multi-line
sweep for a fallback operator wrapped onto the following line — the form that
was missed on this exact family — returns nothing else, and the deprecated flat
`schema.pageSize` shorthand that `ObjectGrid` also reads has **zero** occurrences
in this file (control: `schema.` occurs 264 times in the same command). So this
is one resolver at one entry feeding six consumers, not four hand-spelled chains.

## ⭐ The reproduction — the card said this part was inferred, and it now is not

Measured in the real renderer (real `ListView`, real `SchemaRenderer`, real
registry, stub leaf) over a twelve-row fixture, before any change:

| authored | measured |
|:--|:--|
| `pagination.pageSize: 0` | `$top: 0` on the wire; nothing came back; the view drew its **EMPTY STATE** — the child grid never rendered at all, so there was no table, no record-count bar and no pager |
| `pagination.pageSize: -10` | `$top: -10` on the wire, same empty state |
| `pagination.pageSize: 25.5` | `$top: 25.5` on the wire; `25.5` became the child grid's `pageSize`; turning the page asked for a fractional `$skip` |
| no `pagination` | `$top: 100` — the fifth default, confirmed |

⚠️ **One consequence the card implies is NOT reachable, and it is the mirror of
the sibling's `Infinity` correction.** The data-limit banner and the
rows-per-page control both live inside the record-count bar, and that bar is
gated on `data.length > 0`. With a size of `0` the fetch returns nothing, so
those two consumers never render at all — the refused value cannot be seen
there. It becomes visible only at a **truthy** invalid size below the row count,
where the rows do come back: at `pagination.pageSize: 2.5` the banner printed
**"Showing first 2.5 records"** to the reader.

## Why refusing these is not this renderer inventing a meaning

`@objectstack/spec` already answers it: the view pagination member is declared a
positive integer with a default, and the spec's own suite pins the refusals under
the names **`should reject zero pageSize`** and **`should reject negative
pageSize`**. The `limit` that this package's `ElementDataSourceMapping` lowers
`pagination.pageSize` into is declared positive as well. So `0` is not a spelling
whose meaning a consumer may choose.

The refusal is **fail-soft on purpose**: throwing would take out the whole list
over one declaration. The value is dropped, this view's own default is used, and
one `console.warn` — on the channel this component already uses for "you declared
it, the renderer dropped it" — names the member and the value. ⛔ Not a silent
clamp: without the loud half, substituting a number the author never wrote is
the quieter half of the same defect. The **runtime** choice is covered too, not
only the authored one — `pageSizeOptions` is authored metadata, so an author can
put a refused number in the control itself, and picking it used to overwrite a
perfectly good authored size.

## The pin, red-first

Against **unmodified** source: `command-exit 1` — **9 failed / 6 passed**. The 9
are the refusal rows (every consumer separately); the 6 are the controls, which
must stay green. After the repair: `command-exit 0` — **15 passed**.

⚠️ **One row passed against the unmodified source on the first draft and was
STRENGTHENED rather than noted.** The record-cap row was written at `25.5`, which
is *above* the twelve-row fixture, so the banner never rendered and the row
measured nothing. Re-pointed at `2.5`, it reddens. That is the same class of
green the sibling card reported, reached by a different mechanism.

## Ablations — five legs, each restored and proved

Every leg mutated the committed source on disk, proved the mutation landed by
**blob hash** against the `HEAD` blob (an empty hash treated as a failure, not a
pass), ran the pin, then restored and proved the restore by **hash equality AND
an empty `git diff HEAD`**. Absolute paths, `trap … EXIT INT TERM`. The expected
direction was stated **before** each run. No build stands between the edit and
the run: the pin imports the component relatively and the root vitest config
aliases this package to its `src`.

| ablation | expected | measured |
|:--|:--|:--|
| resolver → the old `??` chain | RED | **RED** — 7 rows: the wire, the rows that come back, the grid hand-off, the window step, the record cap, the rows-per-page path |
| diagnostic forced to stay silent | RED on the 2 diagnostic rows only | **RED** — exactly those 2; every control green |
| diagnostic made unconditional | RED on the valid-value silence control | **RED** — exactly that 1; the absent-key control green |
| predicate drops its integer check | RED on the non-integer rows only | **RED** — 5 rows, all fractional; the zero and negative rows green |
| resolver drops the runtime-choice precedence | RED on the rows-per-page rows | **RED** — exactly those 2 |

⭐ **The value choice is the sibling's lesson applied, and it lands differently
here.** objectui#9853's flat site used `||`, where `0` was already falsy, so no
assertion about `0` could redden it and the pin had to be rebuilt on
truthy-invalid values. At **this** view's single read point the operator is `??`,
which passes `0`, `-10` and `25.5` alike — so all three disagree with the
resolver and all three are pinned. The truthy-invalid rows are kept regardless,
because they are the ones that reach the screen instead of being swallowed by an
empty state, and the integer-check ablation shows they are separately pinned.

⭐ **A green worth reporting.** The first ablation reddens **7** rows where the
unmodified source reddened **9**. That is not a hole: it ablates the resolver
half only, and the diagnostic half is a separate function that still fires. The
pin's 9 red-first rows decompose cleanly into 7 (resolver) + 2 (diagnostic), and
the second and third legs cover the diagnostic conditional in **both**
directions.

## Verification

All heavy runs through the shared lock; VERDICT lines read, never a bare `$?`.

| run | VERDICT |
|:--|:--|
| the new pin on **unmodified** source (the reproduction) | `command-exit 1` — 9 failed / 6 passed |
| the new pin after the repair | `command-exit 0` — 15 passed |
| `packages/plugin-list/` full suite | `command-exit 0` — **81 files, 994 tests** |
| dependency-closure build (a type-check prerequisite) | `command-exit 0` |
| `@object-ui/plugin-list` `type-check` | `command-exit 0` — both legs, `tsconfig.test.json` included |
| every cross-tree test that reads this file's bytes | `command-exit 0` — **12 files, 327 tests** |

`eslint .` in this package: **exit 0** — 0 errors, 528 warnings (all pre-existing
classes). Gates, all exit 0: `check-changeset-presence`,
`check:new-line-citations`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:changeset-claims`,
`check:pending-changeset-literals`, `changeset:check`, `check:control-bytes`.
`check-governed-queue-guard --test` on all three paths: **NOT GOVERNED**.

Readings anchored to `f890c0e39`, the final commit of this branch.

## Sweeps

**Cross-tree.** Every test anywhere that reads this file's bytes was enumerated
and run (`app-shell`, `core`, `plugin-calendar`, `plugin-grid`, `plugin-list`,
`react`, `types`, `scripts`) — 12 files, 327 tests, green. Separately, the tree
was swept for any test that **authors** a non-positive or non-integer page size:
exactly **two** files do, the sibling's pin and this one (control: 87 files
author some `pageSize`). So no other test's behaviour can move on this change.

**Pending changesets.** `check:changeset-claims` named **7** pending bodies that
mention this file. All seven were read in full; none is falsified. Six describe
the gantt render branch, the kanban adapter's `groupField`, the generated
`object-kanban` node's `groupBy`, and the `userActions` harvest — this diff
changes **0** lines matching any of `gantt`, `kanban`, `userActions`,
`groupField`, `groupByField` (control: 7 changed lines match `pageSize`). The
seventh describes its own comment-pair edit and is not about this tree.

## ⛔ What this does NOT do — and why

- **The fifth default is declared, not settled.** The literal is now a named
  constant, so its divergence from `ObjectGrid`'s own three is a stated choice
  rather than a by-product. It is **not** collapsed to one number: changing it
  changes what every list with no authored `pagination` fetches, which is a
  product decision and not an execution seat's. Handed back on the issue.
- **No spec change.** The declaration-side half is another repository's and is
  filed there. ⚠️ Noting a discrepancy this seat could not settle from here: the
  card body names that half as objectstack#18972 while the dispatch and the claim
  comment name objectstack#19046. Both are outside this fence; flagged, not acted on.
- **A SIXTH site of this class, reported and not touched.** `savedViewLimit` in
  `packages/core/src/data-scope/element-data-source.ts` admits a saved view's
  `pagination.pageSize` on `typeof … === 'number'` alone, so `0`, `-10` and
  `25.5` lower into the composed `limit`; and `ObjectKanban` spends that limit as
  `$top: schema.limit ?? DEFAULT_KANBAN_LIMIT` — the same `??`, a sixth default.
  Both are outside this fence and are reported for triage, not repaired here.
- **No labels, no readiness, no merge.** Left in **draft** for the seat.
